query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Calphad-based computational thermodynamics can accurately predict the melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Calphad-based computational thermodynamics modeling with key parameters: alloy composition, temperature range, and thermodynamic database
generation.conditions: Alloy composition: multi-principal element alloys, Temperature range: 298-2000 K
generation.predicted_outcome: Melting temperature within 10 K, enthalpy and entropy of fusion within 5%, volume change at melting within 2%, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties within 5% of experimental values
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in thermodynamic database, limitations in Gibbs free energy minimization method

falsification_experiment.design: Experimental measurement of melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties for a set of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the average absolute deviation between predicted and experimental values exceeds 15% for any of the measured properties, the hypothesis is falsified
